$comment: What the bake-off can compare (docs/voice-bakeoff.md). `models` is the researched list (checked 2026-10-27, sources in the doc). The page's model picker shows it before a key is entered, then the provider's own live list once one is. `tags`: has inline expression (bracketed audio tags on ElevenLabs v3+ and Gemini 3.1, angle-bracket vocal tags plus a style field on Gemini 3.8); `context`: takes previous_text/next_text; `dialogue`: has a one-request multi-speaker mode; `instruction`: takes delivery as director's notes in a prompt (Gemini 3.1; 3.8 would read them aloud). `presets` are the columns a fresh page starts with, and what the command line renders. `fake` makes tones so the page can be tried with no keys.

models.label: Eleven v4
models.about: Newest. Built for expressive long-form narration; follows free-form audio tags ([sighs], [whispers], [long pause]). No SSML.

models.label: Eleven v4 Turbo
models.about: v4 for real-time use, at half the price.

models.label: Multilingual v2
models.about: Steady and proven. No audio tags: pauses go in as SSML breaks, and it takes neighboring lines as context.

models.label: Flash v2.5
models.about: Lowest latency and cost. No audio tags: pauses go in as SSML breaks.

models.label: Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS
models.about: Newest Flash TTS. Speaks every word it is sent, so style rides in speechMetadata and beats in <angle brackets>. Two-speaker mode.

models.label: Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS (preview)
models.about: The first Gemini TTS with audio tags: [bracketed] tags under an audio profile and director's notes.

models.label: Fake tones
models.about: No key, no voice: a tone as long as the words. For trying the page.
